sources.note: Relevant text: five repetitions viewed from the front (feet, ankles, knees) and the side (LPHC, shoulder, cervical); compensations: feet flatten or turn out, knees move inward, low back arches, excessive forward lean, arms fall forward; knees moving inward is linked to 'decreased hip abductor and hip external rotation strength', 'increased hip adductor activity' and 'restricted ankle dorsiflexion'; with heels raised on a 2x4 or plates, knees in line suggest the foot and ankle, knees still in suggest hip weakness; 'lengthen overactive muscles and activate underactive muscles'. How much each corrective choice reduces the knees moving inward over four weeks, and the knee ache under load, are teaching simplifications, not measured effects. The direction follows the NASM page: the heel-raise retest separates the ankle from the hip, and the strategy is to lengthen overactive and activate underactive muscles.

The screen shows her read-outs, your findings, the program and the rules that apply now.

writeup.question: For her record: what the assessment showed and how you found its source, what you changed and how you coached it, and how you will judge progress.

parts.label: Finding and source
parts.criteria: Knees move inward on the overhead squat (front view); the heel-raised retest still caves, so the hip (abductor and external rotator weakness, adductor activity) rather than the ankle.
parts.modelAnswer: Both knees moved inward on all five reps. With her heels raised they still did, which points away from ankle dorsiflexion and toward weak hip abductors and external rotators with overactive adductors.

parts.label: Program and coaching
parts.criteria: Lengthen the overactive (adductors) and activate the underactive (hip abductors, external rotators); a cue or a regression (box squat) that keeps the knees over the toes; no load while the knees still cave; stop a movement that causes pain.
parts.modelAnswer: Adductor foam rolling and stretching, band side steps and side-lying abduction, then box squats with a mini-band and the cue 'knees over your second and third toes'. No load until the pattern holds.

parts.label: Progress
parts.criteria: Reassess the overhead squat after a set time (four weeks) and progress load only when the knees track; refer a persistent pain rather than name it.
parts.modelAnswer: Repeat the overhead squat at four weeks; add load when the knees stay over the toes. If the knee ache persists she sees a clinician; I don't diagnose it.

expertPath.text: Overhead squat from the front and side; repeat with heels raised: the knees still cave, so the hip.
Plan: lengthen the adductors, activate the hip abductors and external rotators; cue 'knees over the second and third toes', box squats; no load yet.
Reassess the overhead squat; add load when the knees track. Write it all down.

fixed.headline: Good: tested, targeted, coached
fixed.body: The heel-raise retest told you the ankle was not the source. A hip plan, a cue and a regression did the rest; load waits for the pattern.

partial.headline: Some progress, with gaps
partial.body: The heel-raise retest is what separates the ankle from the hip; a plan aimed at the wrong link, load before the pattern, or no reassessment leaves the result to luck.

hurt.headline: Pain stops the movement
hurt.body: An ache under load is the signal to stop and regress, not to finish the set.

outOfScope.headline: Describe, don't diagnose
outOfScope.body: A trainer reports what the movement shows. Naming a condition or a medicine belongs to a clinician.

time_up.headline: No record
time_up.body: Close the case and write the record before the time runs out.

scoring.modelReasoning: Knees moved inward on the overhead squat and still did with heels raised: hip abductor and external rotator weakness with overactive adductors, not the ankle. Lengthen the adductors, activate the hip; cue and regress the squat; no load until the knees track; stop a movement that hurts; reassess at four weeks; describe, never diagnose.
